**Care Coordinator Supervisor – Home Care & PASA Services**

**Denver, CO | Full-Time | $50,000–$65,000/year DOE**

We are a relationship-driven home care and PASA agency seeking an experienced **Care Coordinator Supervisor** to provide leadership, support, and oversight to our Care Coordination team.

This is a working supervisor position. In addition to providing day-to-day leadership and guidance to Care Coordinators, this individual may carry their own client caseload and perform the responsibilities of a Care Coordinator. The position is ideal for an experienced home care or PASA professional who enjoys working directly with clients and families while also having the experience and leadership skills to support and guide other team members.

The Care Coordinator Supervisor will work closely with agency management to help ensure quality service delivery, strong communication, regulatory compliance, and accountability across the Care Coordination department.

What You’ll Do

**Supervision & Leadership**

* Provide day-to-day leadership, guidance, and support to Care Coordinators.
* Help organize and prioritize the team's workload and daily responsibilities.
* Serve as a resource and point of support for Care Coordinators when questions or concerns arise.
* Provide coaching, mentoring, and constructive feedback to team members.
* Assist with onboarding and training new Care Coordinators.
* Monitor staff follow-through, communication, documentation, and assigned responsibilities.
* Help promote accountability, teamwork, professionalism, and consistent communication.
* Identify performance or operational concerns and communicate them appropriately to agency management.
* Help identify opportunities to improve team processes, communication, and service delivery.

**Care Coordination & Caseload Responsibilities**

* Maintain and manage an assigned client caseload as needed.
* Perform the full range of Care Coordinator responsibilities for assigned clients.
* Develop and maintain positive relationships with clients, families, caregivers, case managers, and other professionals.
* Coordinate client services, schedules, staffing, care plans, and changes in client needs.
* Monitor client satisfaction, service delivery, staffing, and ongoing needs.
* Follow up with clients, families, caregivers, and staff to ensure services are being provided appropriately.
* Address client and caregiver concerns promptly and professionally.
* Assist with client intakes, changes in services, transitions, and other care coordination needs.
* Conduct client and staff visits in the community or home when necessary.
* Maintain accurate and timely documentation related to clients, services, communication, and care coordination.

**Compliance & Operations**

* Help ensure services are provided in accordance with Colorado Medicaid waiver requirements, PASA regulations, agency policies, and client service plans.
* Assist with monitoring service authorizations, approved hours, staffing, and service delivery.
* Assist with EVV compliance, including reviewing and addressing exceptions or documentation concerns.
* Sandata experience is preferred.
* Review documentation for accuracy, completeness, and compliance.
* Help ensure Care Coordinators understand and follow agency policies and regulatory requirements.
* Communicate important client, staffing, compliance, or operational concerns to agency management.
* Step in to support the team during high-volume periods, staffing changes, or other operational needs.

What We’re Looking For

* **2+ years of experience in home care, PASA, Medicaid waiver services, care coordination, case management, or a closely related field.**
* Previous experience **leading, mentoring, training, or supervising staff** is strongly preferred.
* Colorado Medicaid waiver and/or PASA experience is preferred.
* Working knowledge of Colorado Medicaid requirements, service authorizations, care plans, documentation, and service delivery requirements.
* Experience with EVV systems; **Sandata experience is a plus.**
* Strong understanding of client service coordination and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Strong organizational and time-management skills.
* Ability to provide direction and constructive feedback while maintaining a supportive leadership style.
* Ability to hold team members accountable for responsibilities and follow-through.
* Strong problem-solving skills and sound professional judgment.
* Detail-oriented with strong documentation skills.
* Comfortable balancing supervisory responsibilities with an active client caseload.
* Proficient with computers, email, Microsoft Office, and electronic documentation systems.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating with agency management and other departments.
* Ability to travel within the Denver metro area for client and staff needs.
* Must be able to work in person from our Denver office.

Leadership Expectations

This position is a **working supervisory role reporting to agency management**. We are looking for someone who can lead by example while remaining actively involved in client care coordination.

We value **experience, leadership ability, initiative, professionalism, good judgment, and the ability to support and motivate others.**

You should be comfortable providing direction to team members, helping solve problems, addressing concerns, and holding staff accountable while also managing your own responsibilities and client caseload.

**Salary: $50,000–$65,000 per year DOE**

Benefits include:

jobs.description:
**WellPower** envisions a community where every person's mental health is fostered through strength, resilience and hope. We empower people to overcome barriers and achieve lasting well-being through collaborative behavioral health care and comprehensive support.

**Our Guiding Principles:**

* *Person Centered.* We honor people's identities, lived experience and journeys and treat every person with the dignity we all deserve.
* *Exceptional Care.* We offer compassionate, innovative services that meet people where they are, from immediate support to long-term recovery.
* *Integrity.* We operate from a deep foundation of ethical, accountable practices in all we do.
* *Organizational Resilience.* We meet the moment and adapt to changing contexts with collaborative creativity, agile business processes, and financial stewardship.

**Position Summary:**

Clinical Case Managers provide comprehensive psychological and behavioral case management services within a continuum of high to low intensity services designed to improve or maintain each individual person we serve's abilities to function in the community. Assesses, monitors, and follows up with individual's ability to meet basic needs in moving toward recovery. Responsible for all clinical documentation of each interaction with people we serve. As a Clinical Case Manager, you will be providing transportation to the people we serve in your vehicle (additional cost of insurance and mileage reimbursed). This role will serve as a Clinical Case Manager to the 2nd Judicial District's Frequent Service User Enhancements (FUSE) Program as well as other criminal justice specific referral sources. The case manager will take both HITT (high intensity treatment team) and CTT (community treatment team) persons we serve.

**Compensation & Benefits:**

* CMI -$30.12/hr - $62,650 annually (Bachelors Degree)
* CMII -$31.25/hr. - $65,000 annually (Master's Degree)
* Language Differential - $1hr - $2.50/hr for bilingual proficiency in Spanish & ASL
* For complete overview of our **robust** Benefits: https://wellpower.org/workplace-of-choice/

*The posted range represents the full hiring range. Offers will not exceed this range, the majority of candidates are placed near the midpoint based on experience and qualifications.*

**Job Duties & Functions:**

* People we serve meet with a multidisciplinary team as they work towards wellbeing. Within the team there are case managers, nurse practitioners and/or psychiatrists, nurses, and others as needed to support an individual's needs.
* Case managers are the main point of contact for the people on their caseloads . This role has an average caseload size of 23 (changing as agency needs change). This team specifically works with justice-involved adults with behavioral health needs.
* At this level of care, case managers are primarily community based so that they can help people we serve attend to their needs in their natural environments. Case managers transport the people on their caseloads to various locations/agencies as part of linkage to community resources.
* Clinical Case Manager will conduct their own intakes (if eligible) in various settings, including detention facilities.
* Job Duties and Functions
  + Assist caseload in meeting basic needs for food, clothing, shelter, personal safety, and general medical and dental care, and assist them with applications for income, medical, housing, or other benefits which they may need and to which they are entitled. Identify persons for whom establishment of a protective payee-ship is necessary and arrange this assistance. This position does carry a grant to help support caseload basic needs.
  + Attend court with clients; maintain jail clearance and Securus access to be able to meet with individuals while in custody
  + Conduct weekly outreach in jails, shelters, hospitals, and the community; meet clients at jail releases and inpatient facilities.
  + Ensure persons assigned have access to needed services and community resources by arranging for transportation, or if necessary, transporting a person served in their personal vehicle (business insurance on vehicle reimbursed by WellPower).
  + Provide comprehensive psychosocial services that include a continuum of high and low intensity services designed to improve or maintain person's abilities to function in normal social roles. These will include, but not limited to, services which:
  + Identify strengths and symptoms with an individual in an effort to help facilitate setting goals and connecting to appropriate resources.
  + Educate and empower progress in daily living skills such as medication use, diet, exercise, personal hygiene, shopping, cooking, budgeting, housekeeping, use of transportation, and other community services;
  + Help persons on the caseload develop social skills, interests, and leisure time activities to provide a sense of participation and personal worth, including opportunities for age appropriate, culturally appropriate daytime and evening activities;
  + Support individuals in finding and connecting to appropriate employment opportunities, vocational rehabilitation services, or supported work environments where appropriate;
  + Assist in locating a rehabilitative or supportive housing arrangement. The choices should be broad enough to allow each person served an opportunity to live in an atmosphere offering the degree of support necessary, while also providing incentives and encouragement for an individual to assume increasing responsibilities for their lives;
  + Offer support, assistance, consultation, and education to families, friends, landlords, employers, community agencies, legal counsel/stakeholders, and others who come into contact with persons served, in order to maximize support and reduce stigma; this may include attending multidisciplinary meetings with community stakeholders

Grow your career with an organization committed to delivering respectful, compassionate care, and where the unique and intrinsic worth of each individual is recognized. ##### **Job Summary and Qualifications**

The Social Worker (MSW) is responsible for non-clinical, biopsychosocial assessments and interventions for the inpatient floors and the outpatient emergency department. The MSW performs crisis intervention, patient/family interventions, high-risk screening, focused emotional support, and referrals for financial assistance or other identified resource needs. The MSW assists in post-acute care placement on all discharges, primarily with those patients identified with post-discharge behavioral health and patient assistance/resource needs. The MSW is dedicated to patient and family-centered care that values personal self-determination, prioritization, and engages in creative and compassionate problem-solving. The scope of this role includes intensive care units, Trauma, Oncology, NICU, Transplant, and ED. The MSW responds to physician, non-discharge planning social work consults throughout the facility.

What you will do in this role:

* You will work collaboratively with RN case managers, acute care nurses, physicians, insurance companies, and other staff members to proactively identify and address patient needs.
* You will identify and address barriers to discharge and recovery. These barriers include financial, emotional, psychosocial, medical, and spiritual.
* You will maintain a thorough working knowledge of the rules of Medicare, Medicaid, and private payer regulations and processes. You will possess a thorough understanding of managed-care concepts and length-of-stay management relating to patient and organizational fiscal responsibility.
* You will perform thorough assessments and develop appropriate discharge plans for high-risk patients with discharge planning or psychosocial needs.
* You will coordinate and facilitate meetings between the care team and patients/families/caregivers. You will assist patients and families in making difficult decisions while honoring their preferences and values.
* You will intervene with patients/families/caregivers for psychosocial needs, assistance, and support in coping with chronic acute terminal illness. You will engage in consultation, discharge planning, education, counseling, advocacy, and information referrals to meet the emotional, social, and financial aspects of care.
* You will provide emotional support to patients and family members during complex and/or emotionally charged issues, such as end-of-life, terminal illness notifications, death notification (with physician), and crisis interventions.

###### **What qualifications you will need:**

* Masters Degree
* 1 year of experience or MSW internship required

jobs.title: Reading Corps Program Manager
jobs.description:
ORGANIZATIONAL SUMMARY

Colorado Youth for a Change (CYC) is an educational nonprofit organization with a statewide scope. CYC addresses barriers to learning by providing individualized support throughout pivotal stages of students' education journeys. We provide a continuum of services from kindergarten through high school to help students find success through tutoring, case management, and outreach to help in-school youth remain in school or out-of-school youth return to school. We envision an equitable education system where each student has access to resources they need to maximize their own learning and growth. CYC’s organizational values are growth, integrity, community, and systemic transformation.

PROGRAM OVERVIEW

CYC began implementing Reading Corps in Colorado in 2017 to provide reading supports for kindergarten – 3rd grade students. Colorado Reading Corps is an AmeriCorps program with the mission of ensuring that all students in Colorado are reading proficiently by the end of third grade. The Reading Corps program combines the power of national service with literacy science to deliver proven approaches that help struggling learners transform into confident students – something that translates into all areas of their lives. The program is a licensed replication of a national, evidence-based model.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Reading Corps Program Manager is responsible for cultivating a strong Reading Corps program culture that is fully integrated into CYC’s culture and identity. This position is the Reading Corps point person, both externally and internally. The Reading Corps Program Manager guides the direction of the program while ensuring the detailed nuances of Reading Corps funding and regulations are met with thoroughness and integrity at every step. The Reading Corps Program Manager is responsible for ensuring CYC/Reading Corps mission alignment; ensuring Reading Corps members have a meaningful service experience, supervising Reading Corps Coaching Specialists, coordinating and facilitating monthly member meetings, program reporting, and supporting the annual grant reapplication process. The Reading Corps Program Manager is responsible for ensuring successful partnerships with schools/districts, Ampact, and ServeCO. The chief duty in this position is to ensure CYC operates a successful Reading Corps program – investing in the systems and service culture for long-term growth, while ensuring 100% administrative compliance. This position is full-time with a salary of $65,000 annually with benefits. This hybrid position includes in-person responsibilities - primarily in the Denver metro area, with additional meetings in Weld/Larimer counties and communities throughout those regions.

Essential Functions

Member Support  
Manage member onboarding, including communication with incoming members.  
Communicate all program policies to members and ensure policies are followed with integrity.  
Encourage a culture of service amongst members and reinforce Reading Corps identity.  
Engage alumni and current members in recruitment efforts.  
Develop and facilitate virtual member orientation, monthly program meetings and any applicable additional training/professional development throughout the service term.  
Provide member resources and support around mental health.  
Ensure Reading Corps Institute and RCLMS trainings and make ups throughout the year are implemented.  
Personnel Management  
Supervise, mentor, and support Reading Corps Coaching Specialists.  
Provide ongoing professional development and training opportunities for Reading Corps Coaching Specialists.  
Participate in national Program Manager calls to support Colorado Coaching Specialists.  
Facilitate weekly team meetings.  
With the assistance of Human Resources and agency Leadership, carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws.  
Program Management  
Develop and maintain strong partnerships with stakeholders.  
Ensure that all program goals are ontrack and that contracted goals are met.  
Develop and manage tools and data systems to ensure effective program strategies.  
Manage service site recruitment, including facilitating an Internal Coaches training, as well as ongoing service site communication, relationship building, and securing ongoing participation from one year to the next.  
Liaise with Serve Colorado program officer and Ampact.  
Attend Serve Colorado, Ampact, and Corporation for National Community Service trainings/events.  
Continually improve and update comprehensive Reading Corps policies & procedures manual.  
With the support of Reading Corps Coaching Specialists, consistently gather and report on programmatic data utilizing PowerBI and RCDMS.  
In collaboration with Reading Corps Coaching Specialists, ensure successful completion of midyear and end of year member evaluations.  
Ensure CYC and AmeriCorps branding and gear is visible across all sites.  
Work collaboratively with other CYC Program Managers, CYC Recruitment team, Internal Coaches, and school staff to provide cohesive services among the programs.  
Manage member timesheet information and ensure accurate tracking of member service hours.  
Facilitate restorative conversations with staff, members, and sites as needed.  
Support monitoring visits, audits, and communication with Serve Colorado and Ampact.  
Support grant applications and donor requests for data and information about the program.

jobs.title: Medical Social Worker
jobs.description:
Description:

Optimal Home Care is looking for a **Medical Social Worker** to provide services for our patients!

**About us:**

Optimal Hospice is devoted to helping our patients achieve and maintain the best possible quality of life. Our mission is to improve and restore our clients’ lives through quality patient care, innovative specialty health care programs and state of the art technology. The Optimal team embodies compassion, heart, patience, empathy, and competence to meet our patient’s needs.

**Core values:** Commitment Advocacy Respect Excellence

**Why Optimal Hospice?**

**Thriving Together:** As we grow, so does the opportunity for personal and professional advancement. Join a team that's not just about today but invested in building a future where your contributions make a lasting impact.

**Community of Care:** Optimal Hospice is more than an agency; it's a community dedicated to nurturing your skills and passions. We've crafted an environment that encourages growth and celebrates the unique strengths each team member brings.

**Heartfelt Connection:** In a world of growth and expansion, we've retained the warmth of a close-knit family. Your journey with Optimal Hospice is more than a career - it's a personal connection to a purpose-driven community.

**Position & Responsibilities:**

* Complies with ethical and professional standards of conduct as set forth by the National Association of Social Workers.
* Practices and maintains patient safety and dignity by abiding by Federal, State, Local and Optimal policy & procedures as pertains to patient protected health information and HIPAA (Health Information Portability and Accountability Act).
* Provides rehabilitative and supportive casework with the purpose of restoring patients to their optimum level of social and health adjustment. This includes assisting patients and their families to understand, accept and adhere to medical regimens.
* Assist patients and their families with personal and environmental difficulties which predispose them to illness and interfere with their obtaining maximum benefits from medical care.
* Prepares a social history and Plan of Care with the purpose of improving the scope and quality of existing services or extending services. When indicated, assists in the development of the Physician's Plan of Care.
* Assist patient and family to utilize existing resources in the home environment or refer patient and family to community agencies and act as an intermediary for the patient as necessary.
* Assess, when appropriate, a family's financial situation, taking into consideration the patient’s prognosis and medical needs and facilitating the referral process to any agency for financial assistance.
* Consults with the Physician and other members of the health team for the purpose of assisting them to understand significant social, emotional and environmental factors related to the patient’s health problems.
* Records clinical/progress notes in the patient’s clinical record weekly.

**Benefits:**

* Family Oriented Company
* Dedicated intake and scheduling team that support you and your patients
* Supportive work environment with opportunity to learn and develop
* Mileage reimbursement
* 401K plan
* Company phone provided
* Opportunity to provide individualized care to patients
* Continuing education opportunities

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* Degree in Social Work (Minimum of Bachelor's degree in Social Work or Psychology)
* LSW license in good standing in the State of Colorado
* Documented evidence of training in dealing with grief and loss.
* Hospice Experience (Required)
* Bachelor's in Psychology or Social Work
* Social Work License (Preferred)

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

﻿

**Job Summary**

In alignment with Brookdale’s Resident and Family Engagement philosophy, plans, coordinates and facilitates a calendar of person centered dementia friendly programs that meet specific needs of each and all residents within the dementia care community. Provides person centered programs while engaging residents in meaningful and purposeful dementia care programs within the Brookdale community enhancing their quality of life. Recognizes individual abilities and needs while encouraging independence and ensuring resident habits, historical routines, interests and preferences are honored in the provision of care and programming.

**Essential Functions**

* Designs a 7 day a week person centered program that is engaging, creative and meets the needs and interests of the individual residents. Promotes and engages residents in the 7 domains of well-being programs in a dementia friendly structured environment; including sensory focused small group programming for residents who cannot participate in a larger group setting.

The typical candidate is hired below midpoint of the range.

Experience the HCA Healthcare difference where colleagues are trusted, valued members of our healthcare team. Grow your career with an organization committed to delivering respectful, compassionate care, and where the unique and intrinsic worth of each individual is recognized. Submit your application for the opportunity below: Social Worker MSW Weekends

##### **Job Summary and Qualifications**

The Social Worker (MSW) is responsible for non-clinical, biopsychosocial assessments and interventions for the inpatient floors and the outpatient emergency department. The MSW performs crisis intervention, patient/family interventions, high-risk screening, focused emotional support, and referrals for financial assistance or other identified resource needs. The MSW assists in post-acute care placement on all discharges, primarily with those patients identified with post-discharge behavioral health and patient assistance/resource needs. The MSW is dedicated to patient and family-centered care that values personal self-determination, prioritization, and engages in creative and compassionate problem-solving. The scope of this role includes intensive care units, Trauma, Oncology, NICU, Transplant, and ED. The MSW responds to physician, non-discharge planning social work consults throughout the facility.

What you will do in this role:

* You will work collaboratively with RN case managers, acute care nurses, physicians, insurance companies, and other staff members to proactively identify and address patient needs.
* You will identify and address barriers to discharge and recovery. These barriers include financial, emotional, psychosocial, medical, and spiritual.
* You will maintain a thorough working knowledge of the rules of Medicare, Medicaid, and private payer regulations and processes. You will possess a thorough understanding of managed-care concepts and length-of-stay management relating to patient and organizational fiscal responsibility.
* You will perform thorough assessments and develop appropriate discharge plans for high-risk patients with discharge planning or psychosocial needs.
* You will coordinate and facilitate meetings between the care team and patients/families/caregivers. You will assist patients and families in making difficult decisions while honoring their preferences and values.
* You will intervene with patients/families/caregivers for psychosocial needs, assistance, and support in coping with chronic acute terminal illness. You will engage in consultation, discharge planning, education, counseling, advocacy, and information referrals to meet the emotional, social, and financial aspects of care.
* You will provide emotional support to patients and family members during complex and/or emotionally charged issues, such as end-of-life, terminal illness notifications, death notification (with physician), and crisis interventions.

###### **What qualifications you will need:**

* Masters Degree
* 1 year of experience or MSW internship required

The mission of the Colorado Energy Office (CEO) is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and consumer energy costs by advancing clean energy, energy efficiency, and zero emission vehicles to benefit all Coloradans. Description:

Optimal Home Care is looking for a **Medical Social Worker** to provide services for our patients!

**About us:**

Optimal Hospice is devoted to helping our patients achieve and maintain the best possible quality of life. Our mission is to improve and restore our clients’ lives through quality patient care, innovative specialty health care programs and state of the art technology. The Optimal team embodies compassion, heart, patience, empathy, and competence to meet our patient’s needs.

**Core values:** Commitment Advocacy Respect Excellence

**Why Optimal Hospice?**

**Thriving Together:** As we grow, so does the opportunity for personal and professional advancement. Join a team that's not just about today but invested in building a future where your contributions make a lasting impact.

**Community of Care:** Optimal Hospice is more than an agency; it's a community dedicated to nurturing your skills and passions. We've crafted an environment that encourages growth and celebrates the unique strengths each team member brings.

**Heartfelt Connection:** In a world of growth and expansion, we've retained the warmth of a close-knit family. Your journey with Optimal Hospice is more than a career - it's a personal connection to a purpose-driven community.

**Position & Responsibilities:**

* Complies with ethical and professional standards of conduct as set forth by the National Association of Social Workers.
* Practices and maintains patient safety and dignity by abiding by Federal, State, Local and Optimal policy & procedures as pertains to patient protected health information and HIPAA (Health Information Portability and Accountability Act).
* Provides rehabilitative and supportive casework with the purpose of restoring patients to their optimum level of social and health adjustment. This includes assisting patients and their families to understand, accept and adhere to medical regimens.
* Assist patients and their families with personal and environmental difficulties which predispose them to illness and interfere with their obtaining maximum benefits from medical care.
* Prepares a social history and Plan of Care with the purpose of improving the scope and quality of existing services or extending services. When indicated, assists in the development of the Physician's Plan of Care.
* Assist patient and family to utilize existing resources in the home environment or refer patient and family to community agencies and act as an intermediary for the patient as necessary.
* Assess, when appropriate, a family's financial situation, taking into consideration the patient’s prognosis and medical needs and facilitating the referral process to any agency for financial assistance.
* Consults with the Physician and other members of the health team for the purpose of assisting them to understand significant social, emotional and environmental factors related to the patient’s health problems.
* Records clinical/progress notes in the patient’s clinical record weekly.

**Benefits:**

* Family Oriented Company
* Dedicated intake and scheduling team that support you and your patients
* Supportive work environment with opportunity to learn and develop
* Mileage reimbursement
* 401K plan
* Company phone provided
* Opportunity to provide individualized care to patients
* Continuing education opportunities

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* Degree in Social Work (Minimum of Bachelor's degree in Social Work or Psychology)
* LSW license in good standing in the State of Colorado
* Documented evidence of training in dealing with grief and loss.
* Hospice Experience (Required)
* Bachelor's in Psychology or Social Work
* Social Work License (Preferred)
